transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi… um, I guess I’m here because my eating has been getting a little out of hand. Not all the time, but after work or class I’ll sit down with my laptop and think I’m just going to have dinner, and then I end up eating a whole takeout meal, plus chips or sweets, and sometimes whatever snacks I have in my desk drawer. It’s… more than I meant to, and definitely more than I’d eat if someone else were there. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
When you find yourself eating more than you planned, do you feel like you can’t stop or control how much you eat once you start?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but once I start, it can feel like I’m sort of watching myself keep reaching for the next thing. Like I’ll be thinking, “Jaime, stop, you have a budget report to finish,” and I’m not even really enjoying it anymore, but I still keep going. Does that make sense?
Do you feel upset, guilty, or embarrassed about these eating episodes, and has this affected your daily life or how you see yourself?

Um… yeah, I do feel pretty embarrassed about it. I try not to make a huge deal of it, because I’m still going to work and school and everything, but it has changed things.

Like, I’ve been kind of avoiding plans with friends or my family—especially things like cooking nights or hanging out around food—because I’m worried they’ll notice, or somehow know how much I’ve been eating when I’m alone. So I’ve been keeping to myself more outside of work and class. I know that probably sounds silly, but… it makes me feel worse about myself, I guess.
Do you usually try to hide these eating episodes from others, and do you feel distressed about your weight or body shape because of them?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to say I’m being sneaky exactly, but I do kind of plan it around when people won’t see. Like I’ll wait until my roommate is out, or if I’m home, until my family has gone to bed.

It’s embarrassing because during the day I think I come across pretty put-together, like I’m trying to be health-conscious and responsible, and then… I don’t want anyone seeing how much I can eat when I’m alone. That feels really hard to admit, but yes, I do hide it.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to control your weight or how your body looks?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t make myself throw up or anything like that. And I haven’t used laxatives for that.

Exercise… I try to be active sometimes, but I wouldn’t say it’s, like, extreme or as a way to “undo” it. At least I don’t think so. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Can you tell me more about how long these eating episodes usually last? Do you find yourself eating a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within a couple of hours, and during those times, do you feel like you’ve lost control over your eating?

Yeah… I think that’s what I’m trying to explain. It’s usually after work or class, when I’m by myself. I’ll sit down with my laptop and think I’m just going to eat dinner or have a snack, and then it turns into… more than that.

Like, I might have a whole takeout meal, and then chips, and something sweet, and then whatever snacks I have in my desk drawer. It’s not really how I’d eat if someone else were there. I don’t know if that counts as a “large amount,” but it feels like way more than I meant to have. And in the moment, it’s hard to stop once I’ve started.
Do you usually feel hungry when you start eating during these episodes, or do you sometimes eat even when you’re not really hungry?

Um… sometimes I am hungry at first, but honestly a lot of the time it’s not really that. Like I’ll have already eaten dinner, and then I still end up going back to the kitchen or thinking about ordering more food.

It’s not like my stomach is empty, exactly. It’s more like my mind feels restless or unsettled, and eating feels like… something to do, or something that quiets it for a bit. I don’t know if that makes sense.
Can you tell me if you often start eating even when you’re not physically hungry, especially during these episodes?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, not every single time, but a lot of the time it’s right after I’ve already had dinner, so I’m not actually hungry in my stomach.

It’s more like I feel kind of restless or unsettled, and then I end up going back to the kitchen or ordering more food anyway. I know that probably sounds bad, but… that’s usually how it starts.
Do you often eat much more rapidly than normal during these episodes, or continue eating until you feel uncomfortably full, even when you weren’t physically hungry to begin with?

Yeah… I think I do keep going too long. I don’t know if I eat faster than normal exactly, but by the end I’ll be really full—like my stomach feels tight under my work pants.

And then I kind of just have to sit there for a while, because if I move around too much or bend over, I start feeling sick. I know that’s probably not great… but that does happen.
Do these eating episodes usually happen when you're feeling stressed, upset, or down, or do they happen more randomly, like just part of your routine?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. I mean, I don’t want to say it’s only when I’m upset, because sometimes it just feels like it kind of happens without me really thinking it through.

There are times when I’ve had a stressful day and then it’s more likely, maybe… but I haven’t really tracked it or anything. So I guess I’d say it’s not completely random, but I also don’t know if I can confidently say it’s always tied to being sad or stressed. Is that okay to say?
Have these eating episodes caused you a lot of distress or affected your ability to function in your daily life, like at work, school, or with friends and family?

I mean… I’m still getting to work and school, so it’s not like everything has fallen apart or anything.

But I guess it has affected me socially. I’ve been kind of avoiding plans with friends or family, especially stuff like cooking nights or eating together, because I get worried they’ll notice something or wonder why I’m eating differently there compared to what I do privately. So I’ve been staying home more than I probably should.

I don’t know if that counts as “a lot,” but it does make me feel pretty isolated sometimes.

This turn supports F50.81 (Binge-Eating Disorder) with descriptions of loss of control, eating beyond planned amounts, and emotional distress. F50.9 (Eating Disorder, Unspecified) is ruled out as the symptoms are more specific to F50.81 and F50.2.

The patient denies engaging in compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, laxative use, or excessive exercise following eating episodes, which makes F50.2 (Bulimia Nervosa) less likely. F50.81 (Other Specified Feeding or Eating Disorder) remains plausible given the presentation of distressing eating behaviors that do not fully meet criteria for a more specific disorder.

These episodes are associated with distress, guilt, and social avoidance. There is no evidence of compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, laxative use, or excessive exercise. The clinical picture remains consistent with both F50.81 (Binge Eating Disorder) and F50.2 (Eating Disorder Not Otherwise Specified), as the distinction between the two may depend on more specific frequency or duration criteria not yet fully established.
